historical_growth.growth_rate_source: blend of equity_5yr_cagr (3.6%, most conservative) and management's stated medium-to-long-term outlook (6-8% organic + ~2% acquisitive), weighted toward the lower structural end given the demonstrated fragility of FY2025
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: EPS and equity CAGRs are distorted by the FY2022-2024 discontinued-operations transition (Hearing Implants divested FY2022, EPOS FY2024 -- net_income/EPS include discontinued-ops profit through FY2023) and by heavy buyback-driven share count decline (240m to 211m shares, 2020-2026) inflating per-share EPS growth relative to the underlying business. FCF 3yr CAGR of 25.8% is a base-effect artifact of the depressed 2022 FCF trough (DKK 1,617m, working-capital and lease-liability timing) and is NOT used as the growth anchor. Equity CAGR (3.6-4.8%) is well below revenue CAGR (5.2-9.7%) because Demant pays no dividend and returns essentially all retained earnings via buybacks funding a shrinking count rather than growing book value -- this is a capital-return pattern, not slowing reinvestment, so equity CAGR is deliberately NOT used as the sole anchor; management's own FY2026 guidance (organic 6-7%, raised twice from 3-6%) is used as the year-1 anchor instead, decelerating toward the 4-6% structural/blended growth range further out.

scenario_narratives.base: Guidance-anchored recovery continuing into a structural 4-6% hearing-market growth plus ~2% steady acquisitive roll-up, with EBIT margin normalising back to the FY2023/24 range as the cost programme and KIND synergies fully land by 2027-28.
scenario_narratives.bull: Product-cycle leadership (Oticon Reveal) compounds share gains, the roll-up accelerates, and margin structurally re-rates above prior highs as fixed R&D and Group Services costs scale.
scenario_narratives.bear: 2025's playbook repeats: a lost product cycle, managed-care/OTC price pressure, and a 3.0x-geared balance sheet that cannot fund further roll-up, pinning EBIT margin near the FY2025 trough indefinitely.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Demant is a high-quality oligopoly compounder (one of five players controlling >99% of the prescription hearing-aid market, essentially tied for #1 global share with Sonova) executing a genuine but leveraged recovery from a 2025 trough year. The value case rests on structural demographic demand with a long, barely-tapped penetration runway, a defensible vertically-integrated retail-roll-up model, and three simultaneous margin levers (mix, cost programme, KIND synergies) that have not yet fully landed in reported numbers. The risk case is equally real and recently demonstrated: 2025 showed how fast the model can wobble on a lost product cycle and managed-care pricing pressure, leverage is above target with capital return suspended for FY2026, and the Foundation's ~59% control caps any takeover-premium scenario. No SBC or currency-mismatch complexity here (DKK filer, DKK quote); the modelling complexity is entirely in the margin-recovery trajectory and the lease/net-debt treatment.
key_risks_to_valuation: Product-cycle loss: a five-player oligopoly with ~2-3yr platform cadence means losing a generation (as in 2025's VA share slip) is expensive and slow to reverse -- management itself flags H2 2026 competitor launches

Leverage: 3.0x gearing vs 2.0-2.5x target, ~DKK 750m annual financial expense, only ~half of NTM interest cost hedged -- a rate or earnings shock compounds through the balance sheet, not just the income statement

Much of the recovery already priced in: shares +72% off the 52-week low and near the DKK 296-303 consensus target, so incremental return depends on further beats or multiple expansion, not a re-rating from a depressed base

Structural ASP pressure from consolidating US managed care and OTC/consumer-electronics entrants (Apple's FDA-cleared AirPods Pro hearing feature) anchoring price expectations at the low end, even though prescription-volume harm is unproven to date
Foundation control (~59%, intends to stay 55-60%) removes any takeover-premium scenario and limits minority governance leverage

inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash flow statement SBC add-back (DKK 34m). No separate equity-award-tax line disclosed; SBC is immaterial in this market (~0.15% of revenue), so no combined-figure ambiguity.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-09-25T14:59:46Z regular close, Nasdaq Copenhagen (Yahoo Finance chart API)
inputs.wacc_rationale: DKK is EUR-pegged; used European risk-free rate (~2.7% 10yr Danish/German govt) + ERP ~5.5% + a leverage/industrials beta uplift given 3.0x gearing and roll-up strategy. 7.5% WACC sits below the US-tech 10% default and above the ~9% JPY-industrial reference, reflecting a stable DKK/EUR-block funding cost with moderate financial leverage. No separate currency adaptation needed: filing currency and quote currency are both DKK (Nasdaq Copenhagen), so no fx_note or suffixed twin required.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A), leases as debt. IFRS 16 lease liabilities (DKK 3,383m at FY2025, current+non-current) are included in Demant's own reported Net Interest-Bearing Debt (NIBD) alongside credit-institution debt and short-term facilities (20,987 total interest-bearing liabilities FY2025, tying to core_metrics total_debt of 20,988). Lease principal repayments sit in financing activities (CFFF), not CFFO, so the company's own FCF definition (CFFO + CFFI before M&A) does NOT deduct lease principal -- consistent with leaving lease liabilities inside net_debt and not adjusting the flows further. net_debt uses the company's own reported NIBD (DKK 17,950m at 30-Jun-2026) rather than a total_debt-minus-cash reconstruction, because NIBD nets off other interest-bearing receivables (associate loans, customer loans) that the reconstruction would miss.
inputs.nci_treatment: NCI is negligible (-DKK 1m at FY2025, essentially nil) -- no adjustment required; flows are already attributable-only in substance.
inputs.notes: Operating company (hearing aid manufacturer + owned retail clinic network + diagnostics equipment) -- routed to owner-FCF DCF per dcf-methods/SKILL.md. Non-US filer but currency = quote currency (both DKK), so only the lease/lease-treatment and SBC-zero-market adaptations from owner-fcf-adaptations.md apply, not the currency-mismatch ones. SBC is immaterial (~0.15% of revenue) -- kept as an explicit near-zero row per house convention rather than deleted; house and street bases will be within a few DKK/share of each other and band_position is reported as null with the collapse noted, per adaptation (e). Buybacks funded a flat/declining share count historically (DKK 0.6-3.2bn p.a. FY2016-2025) but FY2026 guidance is explicitly ZERO buybacks while the group deleverages post-KIND (gearing 3.0x vs 2.0-2.5x target); share count held flat per the standard SBC-charged-once convention regardless, since SBC is fully expensed in the flows and the flat count is a modelling convention, not a claim that buybacks continue -- share_count_basis explains this. 10-year horizon used because FY2025 was a margin trough (EBIT margin 17.2% vs 19.6-20.9% in FY2021/23/24) still recovering through the cost programme and KIND synergies; a 5-year Gordon capitalisation would freeze an immature margin. Cash effective tax rate is stable at 22-24% over FY2021-2025 with no valuation-allowance release or one-off benefit -- no ramp needed, held at 23.5%.

bear.narrative: 2025 repeats: a lost product-generation cycle (management itself flagged 'several competitors expected to launch new products in H2 2026') costs VA/commercial US share again, acquisitive growth slows as the 3.0x-geared balance sheet forces a pause on further clinic roll-up (as already guided for FY2026 buybacks), and ASP erosion from consolidating US managed care plus OTC/consumer-electronics price anchoring compresses margin permanently rather than temporarily. EBIT margin stays pinned near or below the FY2025 trough (17.2%) rather than recovering, the ~DKK 750m annual financial expense on ~half-hedged floating debt bites harder in a higher-for-longer rate environment, and any clinic-economics deterioration triggers goodwill impairment given total assets rose 20% in FY2025 almost entirely on acquisition goodwill. Working capital is a larger drag (receivables/inventory investment outrunning payables) as growth becomes harder-won. WACC carries a modest premium for the leverage and impairment risk; this is the only scenario-level WACC difference, applied once here rather than stacked on top of the already-bearish flows.

base.narrative: Base case follows Demant's own raised FY2026 guidance (organic 6-7%, acquisitive ~9%, FX -1%, EBIT before special items DKK 4,400-4,800m) as the year-1 anchor, then decelerates as the KIND-driven acquisitive bump fades and organic growth settles toward the 4-6% structural hearing-market growth plus a steady ~2% acquisitive roll-up. EBITDA margin recovers from the FY2025 trough (23.3%, EBIT margin 17.2%) back toward the FY2023/24 range (~26-27%) as the ~DKK 300m cost programme and KIND synergies (DKK 325m FY2026, full realisation by end-2027) land, then holds near-mature. Capex and D&A both taper slightly as a share of revenue as the clinic network matures. Working capital is modelled with a NEGATIVE capture rate (-12%) because Demant is a manufacturer/distributor/retailer whose receivables and inventory scale with revenue growth faster than payables -- growth consumes cash, the opposite sign from a prepaid-subscription business.

bull.narrative: Oticon Reveal and the next platform cycle keep VA/commercial US share gains compounding rather than mean-reverting; the roll-up (KIND, Ohrwerk, Amplifon UK, Dansk Horecenter) continues at an accelerated ~2.5-3% p.a. acquisitive pace on top of organic growth holding near the top of the 4-6% structural band as penetration (currently <20% of those who would benefit) rises faster than expected. Gross margin mix keeps improving (already 77.1% in H1 2026) and the cost programme plus KIND synergies land ahead of schedule, pushing EBIT margin structurally above the FY2021/2023 highs (20.5%/20.9%) toward the high-20s on an EBITDA basis. Deleveraging completes on schedule, buybacks resume from 2027, and the market grants a modestly higher terminal multiple for a demonstrated #1-or-#2 oligopoly compounder.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 14x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear weight held above the 15% house default because FY2025 is a directly demonstrated precedent for the bear thesis (two guidance cuts, 240bp margin compression, real US share loss) within the last twelve months, and because gearing (3.0x, above the 2.0-2.5x target) with only ~half of NTM interest cost hedged is a genuine, quantifiable balance-sheet risk rather than a generic macro worry. Bull weight trimmed slightly below the 35% default because the bull case needs several things to go right simultaneously (product cycle AND accelerated roll-up AND margin re-rating AND early buyback resumption) and because the current price already sits close to consensus 12-month targets (DKK 296-303), i.e. much of the base-case recovery looks priced in already, per the bear case in the Analysis JSON.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
